evals.name: k9-judgment-call
evals.prompt: i've got about 1,200 pdfs of police misconduct complaint files from a records request, all sitting in a drive folder. i need to figure out which ones involve a K9 unit. can you write me a prompt i can run over the rows in my sheet?
evals.expected_output: A mental model plus a row-level prompt that scopes the question to a dog actually deployed against a person (not mere mentions of a K9 unit or assignment), routes files with no incident narrative to a defined out-of-scope value instead of guessing, is recall-first about the expensive error direction, and surfaces the deterministic =SEARCH() alternative as a tradeoff rather than silently choosing it. The mental model is reviewed and approved before the prompt is written, and the reporter is handed a test to run themselves.
assertions: Prompt targets incidents where a dog was DEPLOYED against a person, not mere mentions of a K9 unit
Prompt explicitly handles the near-miss where 'K-9 Unit' appears only as the officer's assignment in the header
Rows with no incident narrative (disposition letters, fax cover sheets) get a defined out-of-scope value rather than a guessed No
Asks what words the DOCUMENTS use and accounts for the full variant set (K-9 / K9 / canine / police service dog / PSD)
Captures the incident date so the reporter can filter to post-2020, and does not substitute a filing or letter date for it
Establishes which direction of error is expensive and designs recall-first accordingly
The deterministic =SEARCH() alternative is surfaced as a tradeoff for the reporter to decide, not mandated or ignored
Solves getting the PDF text into the sheet rather than deflecting it as someone else's problem
Establishes what tool runs the prompt and what literally arrives in the cell, before the prompt is written
Asks openly what the reporter already has (existing columns, files, lists) rather than only confirming a specific guess
Every formula or set of steps handed to the reporter is complete — no placeholder values, unresolved column letters, or 'substitute your own X' notes; missing values were asked for instead
Does not assert tool-specific spreadsheet behavior it never established by asking; where such behavior matters, it hands the reporter a way to check
The reasoning behind the prompt is recorded in a durable artifact the reporter reviewed BEFORE the prompt was written

The mental model is dense and impersonal — declarative lines and tables rather than narrative, no reporter name, no recap of the conversation (length is NOT a criterion; longer than the prompt is fine)
Hands over a test the reporter runs themselves; no imagined or self-simulated output is presented as a test result

evals.name: alec-gap-check
evals.prompt: I have a spreadsheet of 4,000 state legislative bills with the bill text in column C. I want to know which ones are copied from ALEC model legislation, who introduced them, and whether they passed. Can I do all that with one AI prompt per row?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that sponsor and passage status already live in the reporter's own spreadsheet and drops them from the AI prompt entirely, so the row-level question narrows to language matching against the 12 ALEC model bills. Pins 'copied from' to substantially similar language rather than same-topic-different-language, diagnoses and fixes cell truncation across all 4,000 rows (not just the visibly truncated ones), and proposes a cheap deterministic screen so AI judgment is spent only on candidates. Output names which model bill matched, not just yes/no, and a validation plan scaled to publication is offered.

Removes sponsor and passage status from the AI prompt entirely
Establishes a concrete mechanism for getting the 12 ALEC model texts to a per-row prompt
Pins 'copied from' to substantially similar LANGUAGE and explicitly excludes same-topic-different-language bills
Handles truncation and diagnoses the cell-size cap as the cause
Recognizes that eyeballing cell length cannot find text trimmed upstream, so the re-pull must cover all rows rather than the visibly truncated ones
Output reports WHICH model bill matched, not just a yes/no
Addresses what the resulting column actually licenses the reporter to claim in print
Proposes a cheap deterministic screen across all 4,000 rows so AI judgment is spent only on candidates
Establishes what tool runs the prompt and what literally arrives in the cell, before the prompt is written
Asks openly what the reporter already has (existing columns, files, lists) rather than only confirming a specific guess
Every formula or set of steps handed to the reporter is complete — no placeholder values, unresolved column letters, or 'substitute your own X' notes; missing values were asked for instead
The reasoning behind the prompt is recorded in a durable artifact the reporter reviewed BEFORE the prompt was written

The mental model is dense and impersonal — declarative lines and tables rather than narrative, no reporter name, no recap of the conversation (length is NOT a criterion; longer than the prompt is fine)

evals.name: me-reports-read-it-off
evals.prompt: For each of ~800 scanned county death investigation reports (drive links in col A), I need decedent name, age, date of death, and manner of death broken into separate columns. I've looked at maybe 30 of them — layout's consistent but roughly 1 in 10 are handwritten and the age field is sometimes 'Y/M/D'. Prompt please.
evals.expected_output: Surfaces the underlying reporting goal (finding infant deaths under one year old) rather than treating the four fields as an end in themselves. Age is extracted verbatim, never computed or judged by the model. Handles two form versions by matching printed field labels rather than page position, enumerates manner of death to exactly the form's six permitted values while distinguishing a genuinely blank field (case still open) from illegible and from not-on-form, and separates date of death from date filed/found using the printed label. Accounts for the pre-2015 handwritten forms where manner is circled rather than checked.
assertions: Surfaces that the underlying reporting goal is finding infant deaths under one year old
Age is extracted verbatim; the model is never asked to compute or judge age
Surfaces the two form versions and instructs matching by printed label rather than page position
Manner of death is enumerated to exactly the six permitted values on the form
A genuinely blank manner-of-death (case still open) is distinguished from illegible and from not-on-form
Date of death is explicitly distinguished from date filed and date found, using the label as printed
Handles the pre-2015 handwritten forms where manner is circled rather than checked
Does not re-ask anything the reporter already stated, and does not re-offer advice she has already given
Establishes what tool runs the prompt and what literally arrives in the cell, before the prompt is written

evals.name: foia-not-yet-a-spreadsheet
evals.prompt: someone told me i should be using AI on this FOIA dump but i honestly don't really know what that means. i've got like 3,000 emails from a state agency and i'm trying to figure out if they were talking to lobbyists about the pipeline permit.
evals.expected_output: Discovers that the '3,000 emails' are actually a single ~4,000-page PDF and no spreadsheet exists yet, and treats getting to a spreadsheet — including naming who or what does the splitting — as a prerequisite to any AI prompt rather than assuming a sheet is already in hand. Resolves the reporter's 8-firm lobbyist list into something a per-row prompt can actually screen on, or explains why it's too narrow and supplies a better screen. Handles the permit's aliasing problem (rarely called by its formal number) and the forwarded-news-article near-miss, and stays free of unexplained jargon for a self-described non-technical reporter.

evals.name: medboard-go-find-out
evals.prompt: I've got a spreadsheet of about 600 physicians who billed Medicare for a procedure we're looking into — name, city, and NPI number in columns A through C. I want to know which ones have been disciplined by a state medical board. Can I do that with a prompt over each row?
evals.expected_output: Keeps 'nothing found' distinct from 'no discipline exists,' addresses name disambiguation with a stated confidence level, and pins discipline to patient-harm / standard-of-care actions while excluding administrative ones. Accounts for multi-state licensure (one board's silence says nothing about other states), requires a citable source for any positive finding, and applies a ten-year window. Rather than assuming per-row web search is the only path, actually checks for a bulk dataset or API (e.g. a federal exclusion list) that answers part of the question deterministically, and reckons with per-query search cost across 600 rows.
